## This week

Why the same model gets different accuracy depending on how it is asked: chain-of-thought externalizes intermediate steps onto the page, few-shot exemplars induce it in context, and sampling many solutions buys accuracy for compute (self-consistency, test-time compute).

The notes open as an ordinary web page (print from the browser to get a PDF); the slides download as a PowerPoint file.

## Lab

`W2_lab_prompting.ipynb` — the same model on the same problems under two prompts (answer only, worked solution first), the silent-thinking and answer-first controls, a code-graded eval improved from a baseline through a format fix to your own chain-of-thought prompt, few-shot email classification, self-consistency by majority vote, and the hallucination limit. In-class practice; nothing from the lab is submitted.

Click *Open in Colab* in the table above. Save your own copy first (**File → Save a copy in Drive**), paste your API key into the setup cell, and run top to bottom. **Prerequisite:** your own API key — follow the [API Setup Guide](api-setup.qmd).

## Homework

`W2_hw_prompting.ipynb` — four assignments in the lab's structure with new tasks: chain-of-thought by instruction, an exemplar that pins an output format, your own chain-of-thought prompt with a five-sample vote, and few-shot chain-of-thought exemplars on a Roman-numeral evalset. Each assignment has one fill-in block and a fixed check cell; the completion cell must print `HOMEWORK COMPLETE`. Run the notebook top to bottom, download it (**File → Download → Download .ipynb**), and upload the file to the LMS before the Week 03 class. Grading reads the saved outputs.

## Presentations

Chain-of-Thought ([Wei et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11903)) and Self-Consistency ([Wang et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171)) — the first student presentations. See the [presentation guide](presentations.qmd).
